scope: Resolve a bounded ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY object-ID profile through the dwg2dxf adapter only when the target is one unique top-level typed entity in the same retained block graph and its final DXF identity is proven during output finalization.

behavior: During writeBlockRecords, build a bounded typed entity inventory across model and named block containers, including expected output record name, section, and owner. Resolve DWG soft/hard pointer codes 4/5 and ODA §2.13 offset-based soft-pointer codes 6/8/10/12 with mapped DXF groups 330/340; owner-role and unknown code/group roles fail closed.

Reject absent or duplicate typed source targets, raw entity handle collisions, BLOCK/ENDBLK collisions, known TABLES/OBJECTS collisions, retained ACDS-history handles, collisions with standard/raster/plot-settings/opaque source-frame maps and identity sets, and collisions with retained ordinal/location indexes before allowing a proxy resolver mapping.

Preallocate each admitted target output handle before any proxy is emitted. The proxy-scoped resolver returns only identities in this plan; the generic resolver used for reactors, XDATA, and other records is unchanged.

Before publication, compare the retained proxy reference snapshot and verify each proxy and each referenced target was emitted exactly once with the planned source-to-output handle, DXF type, section, and owner. A missing target emission rejects the complete output transaction.
The plan is export-scoped and cleared on success or failure. Same-adapter correction/retry rebuilds the inventory and output bindings from the live typed model.

validationProfile.source: Locally authored DRW_ProxyEntity and LINE records assembled in memory; all temporary DXF outputs are created under the system temp directory and removed by the test. No DWG/DXF fixture was added.
assertions: Missing target, duplicate typed target, raw entity collision, TABLES collision, ACDS-history collision, standard/raster/plot-settings/opaque frame-map and identity-set collisions, raster/standard ordinal and location-index collisions, owner-role codes 2/group 350 and 3/group 360, and unknown code 7/group 330 each refuse atomically and preserve an existing destination.

Pointer codes 4/group 330 and 5/group 340 plus offset-based soft-pointer codes 6/8/10/12 (all group 330) resolve to preallocated output handles and match the corresponding typed LINE handles after a fresh ASCII/Binary readback. DXF readback canonicalizes offset forms to group-330 code 4.
A target that is present during planning but deliberately omitted by an adapter override fails during finalization, preserves the destination, and succeeds on corrected same-adapter retry.
A proxy reference changed after graph planning is rejected before output publication; restoring the planned references allows the same adapter to retry successfully.
A no-reference proxy profile still passes the existing class-ordinal/payload readback and corrected retry assertions.

validation.fixturePolicy: No DWG/DXF fixture files were added or committed.

authorities.title: Autodesk ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY DXF reference
authorities.use: Defines the proxy entity's object-ID DXF group-code roles; this receipt tests only the mapped 330/340 pointer profile.

authorities.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, section 2.13
authorities.use: Defines codes 6/8/10/12 as offset-based soft-pointer references; the adapter resolves their absolute targets and DXF canonicalizes them to group 330.

authorities.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, section 20.4.90
authorities.use: Identifies the proxy's trailing object IDs as handle references; parser and writer mapping are shared, but this generated control does not prove physical producer fields or semantic closure.

limitations: Generated adapter graph transport only. It does not establish independent physical DWG producer coverage, third-party consumer acceptance, or native proxy semantics.
DWG handle codes 2/3 (owner-role groups 350/360), nested subentities, raw targets, OBJECTS targets, and recursively required target dependencies remain unqualified or refused.
Unknown proxy data slots, EED/common references, mixed proxy/ACDS graphs, complete source-document qualification, and support-claim promotion remain open.
